hero.h1: Agentic Regulatory Compliance Assistant and Document Management Portal on Azure

cta.text: CONTACT US TO AUTOMATE COMPLIANCE RESEARCH

client.name: Food Verification and Certification Company
description: The company is a leading North American provider of independent, third-party food verification and certification services. It works with food producers, ranchers, processors, and retailers across the United States and Canada. Its organic certification team administers USDA National Organic Program (NOP) certifications, helping farms, handlers, and processors achieve and maintain organic certification under federal organic regulations.

customer.heading: The Customer
paragraphs: The company certifies under several distinct standards at the same time. Before this project, it had no centralized system to store, organize, or control access to the regulatory and program documents behind those standards. Finding a specific document often depended on knowing who to ask.
Certifiers, sales representatives, auditors, and administrators each felt the impact differently:
bullets: Certifiers spent significant time reading through NOP regulations and guidance materials to answer questions from organic operations and internal teams.
Sales representatives needed simple, producer-friendly explanations of certification requirements but were handed the same dense regulatory documents used by certifiers and auditors.
Confirming whether a NOP guidance document or policy memo was the current binding version or had been superseded required manual cross-referencing across USDA publications.
Contradictions between binding NOP regulations and interpretive USDA guidance memos weren't flagged automatically, creating audit and certification risk.
Adding newly published USDA regulations, policy memos, and program updates to the knowledge base was manual, unstructured, and slow.

needs.heading: What The Company Needed
needs.intro: The company needed a unified platform that could:

items.text: Centralize regulatory documents across every certification standard
Enforce fine-grained access control down to the folder level
Keep storage, metadata, registry, and search automatically in sync
Deliver cited, natural-language answers to regulatory questions
Give administrators a faster, conversational way to manage the platform

solution.heading: Folio3 Solution
solution.intro: Folio3 built a Document Management and Access Control Portal with an Agentic Regulatory Compliance Assistant on Microsoft Azure, delivered as a self-service web application with a companion Microsoft Teams bot.

groups.heading: Document Management and Access Control Portal

items.label: React
items.text: React, TypeScript, and Vite for the Documents, Upload, and Admin experiences

items.label: Entra ID
items.text: Microsoft Entra ID with MSAL.js for login, with app roles and security groups driving authorization

items.label: Data Lake
items.text: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 as the centralized document repository

items.label: Azure SQL
items.text: Azure SQL Database as the registry of every standard, sub-group, member, tier, and permitted folder path

items.label: AI Search
items.text: Azure AI Search as the index for each document's extracted content, embeddings, and metadata

items.label: AI Foundry
items.text: Azure AI Foundry Agent as the primary assistant for regulatory Q&A

items.label: AI Search
items.text: Azure AI Search for hybrid retrieval (keyword, vector, and semantic)

items.label: Azure OpenAI
items.text: Azure OpenAI (GPT-4o and text-embedding-3-small) for answer generation and embeddings

items.label: Document Intelligence
items.text: Azure AI Document Intelligence for automated text extraction ahead of indexing

items.label: Cosmos DB
items.text: Azure Cosmos DB for per-user conversation history

items.label: AI Foundry
items.text: A second Foundry Agent with MCP tools for conversational administration

items.label: Teams
items.text: Microsoft Teams via Azure Bot Service as a direct channel alongside the web portal

steps.title: Onboard a Certification Standard

groups.label: Administrators create a new standard in a single guided action. The portal automatically provisions:
bullets: The standard's security groups
A dedicated storage folder with baseline permissions
The standard's registry entry

steps.value: A new standard's document library and access foundation are ready in one step, with no manual setup across storage, identity, and access systems.

steps.title: Upload and Structure Regulatory Documents

groups.label: Administrators upload documents and tag each with:
bullets: Category and authority level
Document type and version year
Current-version status

groups.label: The portal also:
bullets: Flags duplicate file names against existing copies
Guides administrators through a replace flow

steps.value: Every document carries consistent, structured metadata from the moment it's uploaded, and duplicate or stale versions are caught before they cause confusion.

steps.title: Grant Fine-Grained, Folder-Level Access

groups.label: Access is governed by:
bullets: A tiered role model (User, Admin, Super Admin)
Per-standard membership
Sub-groups scoped to specific folder paths within a standard

groups.label: Every grant or revoke propagates together across:
bullets: Storage ACLs
Blob access metadata
The registry
The search index

steps.value: Access is restricted to exactly the right subset of a standard's documents, and direct storage access, document listings, and AI search results never disagree.

steps.title: Browse, Preview, and Download Governed Documents

groups.label: Users work directly with the document library to:
bullets: Browse documents across their authorized standards
Preview and download copies

steps.note: All under the same access rules enforced everywhere else in the system.
steps.value: Teams self-serve against the library, not only through chat, with access boundaries enforced consistently either way.

steps.title: Ask Natural-Language Questions with Grounded Citations

groups.label: Certifiers, sales representatives, and auditors ask questions in plain English. The assistant:
bullets: Retrieves content through hybrid keyword, vector, and semantic search
Scopes results to the standards and folders each user is authorized to see
Generates answers grounded in, and cited back to, the governed library
Ranks sources by authority level, separating binding NOP rules from advisory guidance

steps.value: Faster, cited answers to regulatory questions, without users needing to know which standard's library a document lives in or what it's named.

steps.title: Administer the Platform Conversationally

groups.label: As an alternative to the Admin screens, administrators chat with the Admin Agent to manage:
bullets: Standards
Members
Sub-group permissions

steps.note: The Admin Agent reports back exactly which actions it performed.
steps.value: Faster, lower-effort administration for routine changes, with full visibility into what changed.

steps.title: Access from Web or Microsoft Teams

groups.label: Users reach the portal and assistant from the web application, or chat with the assistant inside Microsoft Teams using session commands to:
bullets: Start new conversations
List past conversations
Switch between conversations

steps.value: People work from wherever they already are, with the same governed content and access rules following them across channels.

impact.heading: Impact & Outcomes
impact.intro: By deploying a Document Management and Access Control Portal with an Agentic Regulatory Compliance Assistant on Azure, the company replaced scattered documents and unreliable access management with a single, trustworthy system of record for its multi-standard certification library.
bullets: Faster resolution of NOP regulatory questions across certifier, sales, and audit functions.
Improved certification accuracy through authority-ranked, citation-backed answers tied to specific NOP sections.
Reduced certification risk through automated detection of conflicts between binding NOP rules and advisory guidance.
A standardized knowledge base with full metadata governance across organic regulations and USDA guidance documents.
Higher certifier productivity by eliminating repetitive manual research across fragmented document repositories.
Consistent access control across storage, metadata, and AI search, with any inconsistency surfaced immediately rather than discovered later.
The ability to scale across certification standards without scaling the manual effort of organizing, securing, or searching documents.
